clue.text: Robert has been ahead in this Olympic event

parts.note: Bob is the short form of Robert, and 'Robert has' contracts to Bob's
to have led is to have been out in front

explanation.surface: Robert has been in the lead throughout this Olympic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robert has' becomes BOB'S, the contraction for 'Bob has', and the apostrophe is ignored; 'been ahead' is LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a sled down an ice track is a Winter Olympics sport.

clue.text: Subtle variation used in old fashion accessory

indicators.note: a variation on a word is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A slight change made to an antique piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges SUBTLE. 'Subtle' reads as an adjective on 'variation' but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle was a pad worn under a Victorian skirt to puff out the back, a period dress item.

clue.text: Having no hair — a feature in brocade

parts.note: bald means with no hair
the chin is one of the features of the face

explanation.surface: A bald patch is a design element in a piece of rich cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means a part of the face here, not a design element. Baldachin is also the name for a canopy over an altar or throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Baldachin is a rich silk brocade woven with gold thread, originally from Baghdad.

clue.text: Philosopher, name in the business, crowned with garland

indicators.note: in a down entry, the garland sits on top, like a crown on a head

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the slang word

parts.note: 'the biz' is slang for show business or any trade

explanation.surface: A great thinker, famous in his field, wears a wreath on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'crowned with' do the placing: in a down entry the garland sits on top. Gottfried Leibniz was a German philosopher and mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottfried Leibniz was a 17th-century German thinker, a founder of rationalism.

clue.text: Little is known about this nightmare, in parts

definitions.meaning: an unknown quantity, such as a contestant whose ability nobody can judge
the word split into its two parts: night (dark) and mare (a female horse)

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'nightmare' into NIGHT and MARE, then swap each for a synonym: DARK and HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider whose abilities are a mystery to others, with each half of the bad dream given a synonym.

clue.text: How Americans address chap that misbehaves inside jacuzzi, for instance

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the American form of address

parts.note: bub is an American way of addressing a man, like 'mate' or 'buddy'

indicators.note: something that misbehaves does not stay in order, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: An American calls out to a badly behaved fellow sitting in the hot tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaves' rearranges the plain word 'that' into ATHT, and 'inside' places it within the American address; 'jacuzzi' is an example, hence 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacuzzi is an example of a large tub for bathing in.

clue.text: African curse once placed on trade union leaders

indicators.note: in a down entry, the curse sits above the letters it is placed on

parts.note: ban formerly meant a curse or anathema

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two following words are taken

explanation.surface: An old curse was laid on the heads of a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the sense of BAN as an old one, a curse; 'placed on' puts it above TU in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples across central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Bit of work? It upset ship's cat

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Disturbed during a task, the vessel's cat knocks things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ERG and IT together into TIGRE in the down entry. 'cat' is the definition, a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a big cat, and the female form is this.

clue.text: On edge in the past, perhaps

definitions.meaning: being on edge is being nervous and taut
the past is one grammatical form of a verb, along with present and future

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the past' looks like a time phrase, but 'the past' is an example of a verb form; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious and strained describes being on edge; past, present and future are verb forms in grammar.

clue.text: It's a mistake consuming joint of meat that's rather salty

indicators.note: the word for a blunder eats the joint, so it goes inside

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a rack of lamb is a joint of ribs

explanation.surface: Gobbling a joint of meat that tastes of salt was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' signals one piece swallowing another. Bish is old British schoolboy slang for a mistake, and 'rather' softens 'salty' to slightly salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is slightly salt, as in an estuary where river meets sea.

clue.text: Tommy willing to persevere

parts.note: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the traditional name for a private in the British army
to be 'on' for something is to be game for it, willing

explanation.surface: A British private is keen to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' looks like a man's name, but in British usage it means an ordinary soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly despite difficulty is to persist.

clue.text: Port in Georgia welcoming you back

indicators.note: the state abbreviation takes the turned word in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the word is turned round, read from its end

parts.note: 'one' is the impersonal pronoun meaning 'you' in general

explanation.surface: A harbour town in Georgia greets you on your return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives ENO and 'welcoming' places it inside the state abbreviation. 'Port in Georgia' looks like one place, but only 'Port' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast.

clue.text: Memorise new play first

indicators.note: the play is placed before the abbreviation, coming first in the answer

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: An actor commits a new play to memory before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says the play comes before N, though 'new' is printed earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise lines is to get them by heart, to study until known.

clue.text: How smooth, they say, and succulent!

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: an exclamation 'how sleek!' means 'how smooth!'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how smooth and juicy something is.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'how sleek' gives the plant's name; 'succulent' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a fleshy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The houseleek (sempervivum) is a fleshy-leaved plant, one of the succulents often grown on roofs and walls.

clue.text: Frenzied dozens rush as a danger becomes apparent

indicators.note: frenzied means wild and chaotic, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A dozen people rush around wildly as a threat looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenzied' rearranges the letters of DOZENS RUSH AS A; 'becomes apparent' only joins the clue together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardousness is the quality of being perilous, the state of posing a risk.

clue.text: Worthless, with number transposed, as part payment

indicators.note: number gives NO, the abbreviation, and transposed swaps its two letters

parts.note: something 'of no account' is of no value or importance

explanation.surface: A worthless sum with its figure switched is paid as an instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is the abbreviation NO, and 'with number transposed' swaps it to ON at the start of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid towards a bill without settling it is paid in partial settlement.

clue.text: Honouring French maid rearing fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, rearing up turns the word from the bottom so it reads upwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A French maid is honoured for bringing up fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns BONNE into ENNOB in the down entry; 'rearing' looks like bringing up but means turning upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage is a way of conferring an honour.

clue.text: Cause of Hector's death? A cold, at first extremely severe

parts.note: a chill is a cold or feverish shiver

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Hector died of a bad cold that was very serious from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Iliad, Achilles kills the Trojan prince Hector. The surface suggests an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the Greek hero Achilles slew Hector outside Troy, so he caused the Trojan's death.

clue.text: I remove restrictions after prisoner's examination

indicators.note: the clue's first words come after the prisoner in the answer

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner; the 's gives the S
to derationing goods is to take them off rationing, freeing them from restrictions

explanation.surface: I lift the curbs once the convict's case has been reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the prisoner first, though printed last. Derationing was the lifting of wartime rationing controls in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful thought about something is a close look at it, a study.

clue.text: I am speaking about maiden without scruples

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the abbreviation for maiden

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
oral means spoken
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: I talk about a young woman who has no morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the first pieces around the maiden. In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, shown as M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no moral restraint is unprincipled.

clue.text: A Latin, I can appear volatile

definitions.text: A Latin, I can appear volatile

indicators.note: something volatile is unstable and changeable, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A hot-blooded Latin admits to a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' rearranges ALATINI. Read as a whole, the clue is a native of Italy talking about their own stereotyped temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Italy is a Latin by birth, and the whole clue is spoken in that person's voice.

clue.text: Aquatic creature — a seal, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: Something swims past that the speaker takes for a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' suggests the sea mammal, but here it is a signet, a seal for stamping wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan lives on water, so it counts as an aquatic creature.

clue.text: Unable to sleep in moving camions

indicators.note: letters that move shift into a fresh order, here the French word for lorries

explanation.surface: A driver can't sleep while riding in lorries on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but gives its own letters; 'moving' rearranges CAMIONS (French lorries, also used in English) into SOMNIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is chronic sleeplessness, so the adjective describes someone who cannot get to sleep.

clue.text: Demonstrated fabric

definitions.meaning: to sit in is to protest by occupying a place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrated' means protested, as in a sit-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who occupy a building have staged a sit-in; the smooth glossy cloth is a type of material.

clue.text: In other words, sneering most when tin's taken out

indicators.note: the symbol is removed from the longer word

parts.note: snidest means most sneering
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Put another way, the most sarcastic comment comes when the tin is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' removes SN from SNIDEST. The answer is Latin, written i.e., meaning 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means 'that is', used to rephrase what has just been said.

clue.text: French cleric assigned to unknown church

parts.note: abbé is the French title for a priest
y is one of the letters used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A French priest is posted to a church nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra the unknowns are x, y and z, so 'unknown' can give Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey church is a large church that belonged to a monastery, as at Westminster or Bath.

clue.text: After all, a terrible selection

indicators.note: a selection is a run picked out from the middle of the words that precede it

explanation.surface: In the end, what a dreadful choice it turned out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' reads as one phrase, but 'After' alone is the definition and 'selection' picks the run out of ALL A TERRIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming afterwards and coming at a subsequent time are the same idea.

clue.text: Learning outcome of round I tie

indicators.note: the result of mixing these letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A cup tie in the first round produces a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcome of' rearranges ROUNDITIE; 'Learning' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, knowledge gained by study.

clue.text: Something to wear just one time

parts.note: single means only one

explanation.surface: A garment you will wear on only one occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is a vest or sleeveless sports top.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment.

clue.text: Later on today, getting drunk after drinking one short

indicators.note: the word for drunk swallows the shortened word, as a drinker takes in a drink

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk

indicators.note: the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: the number word as written

explanation.surface: A drinker plans to get drunk this evening after taking one too few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of 'one', and 'drinking' sets the result inside the word for drunk; 'getting' and 'after' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the later part of the present day.
